posts.headline:
LP lock is the pad.
Wallet lock is *ArcFlow*.
posts.lead: The pool cannot be pulled. That is the launchpad's job. Whether the dev wallet can sell tomorrow is ours.
posts.tweet:
LP lock is the pad.
Wallet lock is ArcFlow.

Locking the pool means nobody pulls liquidity.
It says nothing about the bag still sitting in the dev wallet.

Two different promises. Only one of them is ours.

posts.headline:
If it is not on
this page, it is
*not locked*.
posts.tweet:
"Dev locked, trust me" is not proof. A screenshot is not proof.

Every ArcFlow position gets a page: amount, beneficiary, unlock time, contract address. Read straight from the chain.

No wallet needed to open it.

posts.headline:
Two locks.
Two *promises*.

columns.title: The pool stays put
items: Says nothing about the dev wallet

posts.tweet:
Two locks people keep mixing up.

LP lock: the pool cannot be pulled. The pad does this.

Wallet lock: the tokens leave the dev wallet and sit under a schedule that cannot move. This is ArcFlow.

A token can have the first and still get dumped on you.
posts.alt: Side-by-side comparison of LP lock and wallet lock, listing what each one actually guarantees.

posts.headline:
No second token
just to *sign*.
posts.lead: Arc settles in the dollar you are already holding. Nothing to bridge, nothing to top up before you can lock.
posts.tweet:
On Arc, gas is USDC.

No second token to bridge before you can sign. No "insufficient native balance" on the one transaction that matters.

You hold dollars, you pay in dollars, it confirms in under a second.

Arc Testnet, chain 5042002.
posts.alt: Large 'USDC is the gas' statement card with Arc Testnet chain 5042002 and sub-second finality noted below.

posts.headline:
Read it before
you *sign*.
posts.lead: Every field spelled out first: type, unlock time, duration, beneficiary, amount, fee. No surprises in the signature.
posts.tweet:
Before you sign anything, ArcFlow shows you the whole lock in plain language.

Type, unlock time, duration, who receives it, the amount, the fee.

Read it, then sign. After that the schedule cannot move, so it is worth ten seconds.
posts.alt: ArcFlow lock preview panel listing type, unlock date, duration, beneficiary, amount and fee before signing.
